steps.path: All Sessions → Resume → a conversation → Resume Session
steps.headline: An active conversation asks directly whether you want to take over.
steps.changed: A conversation active on your laptop now leads straight to Take over, instead of making you retry first.
steps.notice: Choose a model first, then decide whether to move the conversation.
steps.risk: An unconfirmed handoff still asks before proceeding. These pictures use simulated computers.

steps.path: Another computer claims the conversation while this computer is opening it
steps.headline: Try again retries opening; it never changes into a takeover request.
steps.changed: Try again retries opening, even after another denial. It no longer leads into a takeover question.
steps.notice: Leave it opens nothing. To request a takeover, leave this attempt and start Resume again.
steps.risk: Retries can keep failing while the other computer holds the conversation.

steps.path: Settings → Backup & Sync → information button → Using the same conversation on two devices
steps.headline: The explanation describes the limits without promising that nothing can be lost.
steps.changed: Replaced the one-device-only and nothing-is-lost promises with the actual handoff and conflict-copy limits.
steps.notice: Offline access stays available. Conflicting chats are not automatically combined.
steps.risk: Recent messages may still be missing after a forced or incomplete handoff.

steps.path: Opening a conversation that another computer is already using
steps.headline: Where should we explain that conflicting messages can become a separate copy?
steps.today: The ordinary handoff asks only whether to take over. The unconfirmed-handoff question already explains separate copies, and Backup & Sync has a short explanation.
steps.problem: Git can merge compatible changes, but competing conversation histories are not guaranteed to become one combined chat. Your earlier question about this was never resolved into a copy decision.
steps.proposal: Keep the ordinary confirmation short. Explain the risk when the handoff cannot be confirmed, rather than showing the same warning for every normal handoff.

options.label: Keep the first question short
options.summary: Keep the separate-copy explanation in the unconfirmed-handoff question and Backup & Sync.
pros: Normal handoffs stay quick to understand.
The warning appears when it is most relevant.
cons: Someone who never opens the explanation may not know about conflict copies until a handoff fails.

options.label: Explain it in the first question too
options.summary: Add a brief separate-copy warning before every handoff.
pros: The limitation is visible before the user starts any handoff.
cons: Every normal handoff carries extra warning text.
The same information repeats if confirmation fails.
